thread:
maria-support: FYI BrightFrame (org bf-238) reports embeddings vectors/sec ~50% drop since ~02:00 UTC. Tokens/sec looks normal. No billing/auth 4xx spike from customer side, they say. Opening here so infra + ML can triage.

olivia-sre: I pulled graphs — gpu-pool-7 shows queue_depth spike at 02:03. p50 latency went 12ms -> 40ms, p95 ~220ms. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/embeddings (link) :eyes:

sam-ops: any 429/500 patterns in front proxy? or auth 401/403?

maria-support: quick log excerpt from the customer's route around the window:
```
[02:01:58] svc=embeddings req_id=abc123 status=200 tokens=120 vecs=1 dur=12ms
[02:03:05] svc=embeddings req_id=def456 status=200 tokens=120 vecs=1 dur=220ms queue_depth=42 kvcache_miss=1
[02:03:06] svc=embeddings req_id=ghi789 status=200 tokens=120 vecs=1 dur=230ms queue_depth=48
```
No 5xx/4xx from upstream in that snippet.

kyle-ml: Interesting. I checked the model routing history — there was a variant flip for that org at 01:52 (embed-large-v2 -> embed-large-v1) during a routing experiment. embed-large-v1 outputs 512-dim vectors vs v2's 1536. That explains the dimension mismatch reports earlier, but doesn't fully explain vecs/sec drop.

kyle-ml: Also noticed a recent autoscaler tweak rolled at 01:55 that changed the default batch_window from 8ms -> 1ms to target lower latency for small requests. That will dramatically reduce avg batch sizes under steady qps and kill vectors/sec while tokens/sec (per-request tokens) stays flat. KV cache miss rate is up ~3x at the same time which amplifies per-request work. :thinking_face:

maria-support: Customer mentioned they re-ingested a dataset at ~01:50 and then started seeing mix of 512 & 1536 dims in their index. I suspect two things combined: variant flip caused some requests to target the smaller-dim model, and the batch_window shrink caused small batches so throughput collapsed. Repro steps I ran locally: 
```bash
# run loadgen to mimic their traffic
./loadgen --org bf-238 --model embed-large-v1 --batch_target 64 --qps 220 --tokens 120 --duration 10m
# scrape metrics
curl -s https://internal-metrics/embeddings | jq '.embeddings_vectors_per_sec, .avg_batch_size, .kvcache_miss_rate'
```
When batch_window=1ms avg_batch_size was ~3 and vectors/sec matched customer drop. When I set batch_window back to 8ms avg_batch_size -> 28 and vectors/sec recovered.

olivia-sre: Confirmed in infra metrics: avg_batch_size drops sharply at 01:55 coinciding with autoscaler change-id 7f2c. GPU queue depth rises because many tiny batches create scheduling overhead. Suggest rollback or route-level override.

sam-ops: Proposed immediate mitigations: 1) pin BrightFrame route to embed-large-v2 to fix dims, 2) override batch_window -> 8ms and max_batch=256 for their route to restore throughput, 3) investigate why kvcache miss spiked (maybe different model variant misses). Anyone able to push the route override?

maria-support: I can push the route pin and batch overrides now for org bf-238. Pushing change to staging then prod. Will message customer after changes.

deploy-bot: Scheduled rollback of autoscaler default (change CHG-9842) to restore batch_window default to 8ms at 03:20 UTC, initiated by sam-ops.

kyle-ml: Longer term: we should not globally shrink batch_window without profiling vector workloads. Action items: add a vectors/sec synthetic check in canary (if vectors/sec drops >20% vs baseline and avg_batch_size < 8 for >5m fail canary). Also add model-variant stability check to prevent half-rolled routing experiments.

maria-support: Customer update: I told them we identified cause (model variant + batch_window) and applied route pins/overrides. Asked if they'd like us to re-ingest any 512-dim items or convert. They want an RCA and ETA for full fix.

sam-ops: I'll file infra follow-up for autoscaler rollout policy. For now keep this thread live until vectors/sec is stable for 30m.

maria-support: Monitoring now. avg_batch_size climbed to ~24 and embeddings_vectors_per_sec recovered to ~95% of baseline after override. Customer is satisfied for the moment. :thumbsup:

kyle-ml: Quick note for triage: when investigating throughput regressions, measure embeddings_vectors_per_sec (not tokens/sec) and avg_batch_size; check kvcache_miss_rate and model_variant history.

maria-support: Saving repro commands and graphs to ticket BF-238-INVEST, will attach logs and timeline. Closing internal triage here but will reopen if reoccurs.
